issues.description: signing_mode_enum derivation complects two booleans into a four-state enum via cascading if/elif
issues.detail: The free function signing_mode_enum() in wallet_request_types.py decodes (is_hex, safe_mode) into a SigningMode through a chain of four branches where the last falls through to CHIP_0002. This is the textbook complecting Hickey warns about: two orthogonal boolean facts about the request are being folded into a single mode via positional logic. A simple data-driven mapping (a dict keyed by the (is_hex, safe_mode) tuple) makes the table of facts explicit, eliminates the implicit fall-through, and removes the need to read all branches to confirm coverage. As written, future readers cannot tell at a glance whether all four combinations are intentional or whether one is a default by accident.

issues.description: sign_message and verify_signature both re-derive message bytes from (mode, message) via parallel if/elif ladders
issues.detail: The same shape of conditional appears in two places: sign_message() encodes (mode, message) -> bytes, and verify_signature() decodes the same. Both ladders are doing one job: 'given a SigningMode, how is the message turned into bytes to sign/verify?' That is a pure function of the mode, and it should be lifted out as a single message_to_bytes(mode, message) helper so the two sites cannot drift. Right now they are duplicated and one already has a subtle asymmetry: verify_signature has an explicit 'else: raise' for unknown modes, while sign_message silently treats unknown modes as CHIP_0002. That divergence is exactly what a single shared function would prevent.

issues.description: sign_message silently defaults unrecognized SigningMode values to CHIP_0002 tree-hash encoding
issues.detail: In chia/wallet/util/signing.py sign_message(), the final 'else' branch handles 'anything not explicitly listed' as CHIP_0002. This is place-oriented thinking applied to an enum: any future SigningMode added will get the CHIP_0002 encoding by accident, producing a valid-looking but wrong signature rather than an error. verify_signature() in the same file correctly raises ValueError for unknown modes. Make both exhaustive (raise on unknown), or use a match statement so mypy/pyright forces coverage. The current asymmetry is a latent bug surface.

issues.description: convert_secret_key_to_synthetic on Wallet is an instance method but uses no instance state
issues.detail: The new convert_secret_key_to_synthetic(self, secret_key) on Wallet calls only calculate_synthetic_secret_key(secret_key, DEFAULT_HIDDEN_PUZZLE_HASH) -- no use of self. Yet the caller in wallet_rpc_api.py reaches through service.wallet_state_manager.main_wallet just to invoke it. This complects 'how to derive a synthetic key' (a pure function of a secret key and a constant) with 'which wallet object you happen to have'. It should be a module-level function (or stay inline as calculate_synthetic_secret_key(...) with DEFAULT_HIDDEN_PUZZLE_HASH). Routing a pure transformation through main_wallet ties the signing util to wallet identity it does not need.

issues.description: verify_signature's docstring still says ':param request:' but the function no longer takes a request
issues.detail: The extracted verify_signature() in chia/wallet/util/signing.py was lifted from the RPC method, which took a single request object. The signature is now five keyword args, but the docstring still reads ':param request: :return:'. Small thing, but it is exactly the kind of residue that signals the extraction was mechanical rather than thought-through. Either drop the docstring or rewrite it for the new value-oriented signature.

issues.description: Variable name hex_message is misleading when mode is CHIP_0002 (UTF-8 string) or CHIP_0002_HEX_INPUT (tree hash)
issues.detail: In sign_message() and the old wallet sign_message methods (now removed), the local variable hex_message holds either a tree-hash digest, a UTF-8 byte string, or hex-decoded bytes. Only one of those is meaningfully 'hex'. The name was carried over from the previous code unchanged. Renaming to message_to_sign (matching verify_signature's message_to_verify) would make the symmetry between sign and verify obvious and remove a misleading name. This is a low-cost simplification that pays back every time someone reads the function.

issues.description: VerifySignatureResponse is imported into a util module, creating a backward dependency from a lower layer to a wallet_request_types module
issues.detail: chia/wallet/util/signing.py imports VerifySignatureResponse from chia.wallet.wallet_request_types. The util module is conceptually below the request-types module, but now depends on it for a return shape. A cleaner factoring returns a small value (a NamedTuple or dataclass local to signing.py, similar to the new SignMessageResponse) and lets the RPC layer adapt it into VerifySignatureResponse. As is, the new util drags the RPC request schema along with it anywhere it is reused -- which is the opposite of the stated goal of 'make signing reusable by other wallet areas'.

issues.description: signing_mode_enum exists both as a free function and as @property on two request classes, with the property delegating to the free function
issues.detail: wallet_request_types.py now contains signing_mode_enum(request) as a module-level function and signing_mode_enum as a property on both SignMessageByAddress and SignMessageByID. The property is one line that just forwards to the free function. That is fine, but it means callers can reach the same answer two ways. Pick one: either keep only the property (encapsulate the rule) or only the function (treat the request as data). Two routes to the same value invites the inevitable third caller who picks the wrong one and a future divergence.

review.summary: This PR is a textbook 'easy' refactor: it lifts duplicated sign/verify code out of wallet_rpc_api into a new util module and removes per-wallet sign_message methods in favor of current_p2_puzzle_hash + a shared signing function. That direction is right -- it moves toward values and away from objects-that-know-how-to-sign. But the extraction is mechanical, not decomposed: the same (is_hex, safe_mode) -> SigningMode and (mode, message) -> bytes conditionals are still expressed as cascading if/elif ladders in two or three places, including a silent CHIP_0002 fall-through in sign_message that does not match verify_signature's explicit raise. A single message_to_bytes(mode, message) pure function plus a small (is_hex, safe_mode) -> mode table would make the underlying facts explicit and remove the drift surface. Smaller residue (instance method with no self use, stale ':param request:' docstring, VerifySignatureResponse pulled into the util module, two ways to compute signing_mode_enum) suggests the change was done one site at a time rather than thought through end-to-end. Net: directionally simpler, but several COMPLECTED conditionals and one PLACE-ORIENTED helper are now embedded in the shared module where they will be harder to undo than they were in the RPC.
